subject: Complex numbers
title: Complex Numbers as Ordered Pairs
subtitle: Building the complex numbers out of real numbers alone, so that i is no longer an assumption, and three other ways to build them.
prerequisite_note: Chapters 1 to 3; ordered pairs; dividing one polynomial by another. University sections introduce rings and quotients from scratch.
objectives: Define the complex numbers as ordered pairs of real numbers and compute from the definition alone.
Prove that (0, 1)(0, 1) = (−1, 0) and recover the form a + bi.
Explain why the construction shows that complex arithmetic cannot lead to a contradiction.
Build ℂ as polynomials modulo x² + 1 and prove the two constructions are isomorphic.
Classify every two-dimensional real number system with an identity: complex, dual and split-complex numbers.
Construct complex numbers modulo a prime and decide when they form a field.

theorems.statement: the pairs (a,0) form a copy of R
R[x]/(x² + 1) is isomorphic to the pairs; evaluation at i has kernel (x² + 1)
classification of 2-dimensional real algebras with identity: C, dual, split-complex
any field containing R and a square root of −1 contains a copy of C
F_p[x]/(x² + 1) is a field iff p ≡ 3 mod 4 (p odd)
